qt: to the Commission Ioan-Rareş Bogdan (PPE) Subject:

Though I welcome the Commission’s dialogue with the Southern Neighbourhood countries on managing migrant flows, I have noticed that the EU’s talent partnerships with Egypt, Morocco and Tunisia aim to attract workers in the transport, tourism, hospitality and construction sectors, in spite of the fact that Central and Eastern European countries are struggling to find skilled labour in these very sectors – an issue compounded by migration to Western Europe. I therefore ask the Commission: 1.
How much has been allocated to the deployment of these partnerships with North African countries and which budget lines are financing these endeavours?
Why is it bringing in third-country workers instead of funding programmes that incentivise Eastern European citizens living elsewhere in the EU to return to their countries of origin?
How does it assess the risk that these migration schemes could lead to social dumping and downward pressure on wages for workers in less-developed Member States?
